blueprint-well-formedness.how: Structural only. It certifies that the blueprint is a well-formed graph over ontology terms — it says nothing about whether the part could exist, work, or bear a load. It is the one law in the set that reaches every part of every organism, and the weakest thing anyone could want to know about any of them.

thompson1917-ch03-07.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
thompson1917-ch03-07.about: the slope of log mass against log length is 3 under isometry
thompson1917-ch03-07.how: The cube law as an exponent, which makes it testable: a measured slope that is not 3 is a measurement of how the organism departs from isometry. E1 is the observation that this project's fish do depart.

altitude-coupling.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
altitude-coupling.about: that the feasible set is downward closed in altitude: feasible high implies feasible low
altitude-coupling.how: Couples the two layers: thinner air both reduces lift and reduces oxygen, so a design feasible at altitude is feasible below it. Useful mainly as a sanity direction on a scenario sweep.

physiology-q10.label: Q10 temperature scaling: the ratio between two temperatures is Q10 raised to their difference over ten
physiology-q10.about: how a rate changes with a ten-degree change in temperature
physiology-q10.how: Proved, no instance: no candidate commits a Q10 and the conditions file fixes 25 C. Every rate in every run is therefore at one temperature, and a design whose selling point is a rate should say which temperature it means.

genotype-developmental-ordering.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
genotype-developmental-ordering.about: that a claimed developmental ordering has no cycle and respects the dependencies declared for it
genotype-developmental-ordering.how: The only law in the set that is about TIME, which makes it the one the time-lapse rests on. It certifies that an ordering is consistent; it does not supply one, does not predict a rate, and says nothing about how long a stage takes. A developmental animation is therefore a declared ordering being checked for consistency, never a simulation of development.

E2.label: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
E2.about: a measured band for the weight ratio
E2.how: A measured band from one species. Outside that species it is a number, not a constraint.

E7.label: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
E7.about: that a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored
E7.how: The other law about time, and the one that matters most for a time-lapse: a part that appears after the organism would have died is not a part. Pairs with the developmental ordering law.

aerobic-power-bound.label: Sustained mechanical power is bounded by oxygen delivery (Fick) times efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.about: sustained flight requires aerobic supply at least the required mechanical power over the efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.how: The law that separates a glide from flight. A lifting surface large enough to hold the animal up says nothing about whether the animal can keep it up, and this is the only law in the set that asks. It takes Fick's principle as a NAMED HYPOTHESIS (fick_aerobic_supply) rather than proving it.

fick-principle.label: Fick principle: aerobic supply is at most eta E Q (Ca - Cv)
fick-principle.about: oxygen delivery as flow times the arteriovenous difference
fick-principle.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: the aerobic bound takes it as its named hypothesis fick_aerobic_supply. Everything the aerobic bound concludes rests on it.

physiology-laplace.label: Laplace wall stress: pressure in a thin-walled vessel is limited by wall strength, thickness and radius
physiology-laplace.about: the pressure a thin-walled tube or sphere can hold, from radius, wall thickness and wall strength
physiology-laplace.how: Proved, with NO INSTANCE anywhere in this project: no vessel radius, wall thickness or wall strength exists for any organism here. It is in this table so that a part it would constrain carries the chip that says which three numbers are missing — a law with no instance is a request for data, and silence about it is worse.

E3.label: Efficiency and O2 delivery lie in the ranges the cited sources support (widened after measured zebrafish)
E3.about: a measured ceiling on aerobic power
E3.how: The empirical input the aerobic bound needs. Measured in fish; borrowing it for an insect or a mammal is exactly the move the clade-scoped tables forbid.

scaling-area-law.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
scaling-area-law.about: area under isometry: A scales as L squared
scaling-area-law.how: If the design scales a lifting or exchange surface by changing a length, this fixes the area ratio it gets — under isometry, which is a hypothesis about the design, not a fact about the animal. The flying-fish audit returns `violated` here for skin and fins, because that fish is NOT isometric: the law is right and the hypothesis is false, which is the useful outcome.

E1.label: Isometry fails within a species
E1.about: that measured fin area does not scale isometrically
E1.how: An OBSERVATION of Cypselurus hiraii, not a law. It is the evidence that the isometry hypothesis in the scaling laws is false for that fish, which is why those chips come back `violated` on that body.

scaling-strength-law.label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
scaling-strength-law.about: breaking load under isometry: it scales as L squared while weight scales as L cubed
scaling-strength-law.how: The reason a design cannot simply be made bigger. Weight grows faster than the cross-section carrying it, so a part that holds at one size fails at another with no change in material or shape.

elastic-similarity.label: Elastic similarity scaling (not formalised)
elastic-similarity.about: scaling that holds elastic deflection constant instead of stress
elastic-similarity.how: NOT FORMALISED. The named alternative to isometry for real skeletons, so its absence is why every scaling chip here says `under isometry`.

fin-length-ratio.label: Fin length over body length (not formalised)
fin-length-ratio.about: fin length as a fraction of standard length
fin-length-ratio.how: NOT FORMALISED as a law; E5 records the OBSERVATION that a candidate's ratio falls outside the measured band, which is provenance rather than impossibility.

E5.label: The observed pectoral/SL range
E5.about: a candidate's fin ratio falling outside the measured band
E5.how: PROVENANCE, NOT IMPOSSIBILITY — its own record says so. A design outside a measured band is unusual, and unusual is not forbidden.

muscle-power-premise.label: Thompson's muscle-power premise P = f p M (retired)
muscle-power-premise.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: a named hypothesis (MusclePowerLaw in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean), replaced for the Studio by the aerobic bound. A chip for it must read as an assumption, because that is all it is.

E4.label: Gills do not ventilate in air
E4.about: a measured ceiling on stored (anaerobic) power
E4.how: The burst counterpart of E3: what a muscle can give for a few seconds. For a glide launch this is often the quantity that matters and the one least often declared.

taxiing-thrust.label: Taxiing thrust on the water surface (not formalised)
taxiing-thrust.about: thrust produced while still in contact with the water
taxiing-thrust.how: NOT FORMALISED. The flying-fish runs needed it and did without it.

scaling-bending-law.label: Bending strength of an isometric member via the section modulus (R9)
scaling-bending-law.about: bending stress in a cantilever as the body scales
scaling-bending-law.how: A wing or a leg held out from the body is a cantilever, and the stress at its root rises with size under isometry. This is the law that should be consulted first by anyone who wants to put a lifting surface on the end of a limb.

walking-pendulum-speed.label: Walking speed as a pendulum (not formalised)
walking-pendulum-speed.about: the speed at which a leg of a given length stops working as a pendulum
walking-pendulum-speed.how: NOT FORMALISED. The locomotion layer reports a Froude number for a walking gait and calls the verdict `reported` rather than a pass, precisely because this is missing.

genotype-pleiotropy-closure.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.about: what a view of a genotype may omit: that the set shown is closed under the declared pleiotropy relation
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.how: A statement about the COMPLETENESS OF A VIEW, not about development. If a molecule is shown as affecting one part, this is what certifies that its other declared effects were not quietly dropped from the picture — which is exactly the failure a per-part panel invites.

genotype-genetic-code.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
genotype-genetic-code.about: what a claimed set of substitutions rules out, given the genetic code
genotype-genetic-code.how: Operates on a claimed edit. For a construct with an unedited donor genome there is nothing for it to operate on, and that is the honest answer rather than a refusal.

gene-regulatory-dynamics.label: Gene regulatory dynamics (not formalised)
gene-regulatory-dynamics.about: the dynamics of a regulatory network
gene-regulatory-dynamics.how: NOT FORMALISED, and it is the hole the whole scale ladder sits over. Nothing in the Lean set connects a molecule to a tissue. The ladder's molecular rungs are therefore LITERATURE, graded and quoted, and the theatre must never draw them in the same colour as a proof.

thompson1917-ch02-10.label: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
thompson1917-ch02-10.about: how minimum flight speed scales with size
thompson1917-ch02-10.how: A bigger animal of the same shape must fly faster to stay up. Combined with a launch speed the design declares, this is often what decides a flight claim.

flight-allometry-law.label: General allometry: measured exponents compose (W = a L^b)
flight-allometry-law.about: minimum speed from wing loading and a maximum lift coefficient
flight-allometry-law.how: The law behind `lifting_area_supports_mass`. It needs a maximum lift coefficient, which is where a design most often stops: the coefficient is a MEASURED property of a real wing, the table of them is scoped by clade, and borrowing one across clades is the failure that table exists to prevent.

flight-climb-glide-law.label: Climb from excess power and the range of a steady glide
flight-climb-glide-law.about: climb rate from excess power, and the horizontal range of a steady glide from a height
flight-climb-glide-law.how: Scope.taxa is `any`: it is a theorem about a model and applies wherever the design supplies the quantities and accepts the hypotheses. That makes it the most portable flight law here — and it is about a GLIDE. Powered flight is a power question and goes to the aerobic bound.

aspect-ratio-induced-drag.label: Induced drag falls with wing aspect ratio (not formalised)
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.about: induced drag falling with aspect ratio
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.how: NOT FORMALISED. Without it, nothing here distinguishes a long narrow wing from a short broad one of the same area, which is most of what a wing design IS.

universal_laws.because: the quantities are there and no check in this run evaluated this law against them
scope.taxa is [Danio rerio], and Mus musculus is in none of them. Its numbers are another clade's.
scope.taxa is [Danio rerio], and Mus musculus is in none of them. Its numbers are another clade's.

chain.requirement: The designed mouse must carry a lifting surface on the forelimb whose area is large enough to support its body weight in flight, and this ladder must say which molecule, pathway, cell, cell-cell interaction, tissue and organ change would produce that surface.

missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A spatially restricted gain-of-function mouse - for example Wnt5a, or Fgf7 and Fgf10, driven in interlimb lateral dermis or in forelimb interdigital mesenchyme - scored for membrane outgrowth, area and span. This run found no record of such an experiment.

missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A bat embryo culture or electroporation system, or a captive breeding colony, allowing loss of function of Wnt5a or of the FGF7/FGF10 axis in the developing plagiopatagium.

missing_rungs.why: The flying squirrel fibroblast-to-keratinocyte interaction (l03) is a CellChat inference from single-nucleus transcriptomes, which the paper itself labels putative and candidate. Nothing fetched perturbs a receptor on the keratinocyte side in any gliding mammal.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Receptor-side perturbation, for example FGFR2 or a non-canonical WNT receptor, in patagium epidermis, with the dermal condensate and epidermal thickness scored.

missing_rungs.why: No document fetched gives any mechanical property of a retained interdigital web or of a patagium: no tensile strength, stiffness, thickness under load or failure point. A membrane that exists is not yet a membrane that bears a body.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Mechanical testing of patagium, and of retained interdigital webbing in the mouse syndactyly models above, against the aerodynamic load implied by the physics layer's 4 m drop.

missing_rungs.why: The ontology layer does not grant the designed organism the structure it needs, so the ladder cannot be named end to end. Querying Ubergraph in this run returned wing (UBERON_0000023) never_in_taxon Glires (NCBITaxon_314147) and never_in_taxon Metatheria (NCBITaxon_9263), while two of the three patagium papers fetched here describe gliding membranes in exactly those clades - a rodent flying squirrel and a marsupial sugar glider. patagium (UBERON_0010856) itself returned no never_in_taxon rows in this run. A mouse is Glires, so per the fetched axioms it is forbidden a wing.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Either an Uberon revision removing or narrowing the wing never_in_taxon Glires and Metatheria axioms, or a decision in this project to land the mouse ladder on patagium rather than wing.

missing_rungs.why: Found by adversarial verification, not declared by the builder. The pathway -> cell rung is occupied by exactly one link, l02, and l02 does not cross it. Its quote reports only that two fibroblast subpopulations (Fp2, Fr) are patagium-enriched by differential abundance and expression; the link's own what_it_does_not_show concedes 'nothing here shows the WNT pathway is required to produce them'. Pathway and cell are joined only by appearing in the same snRNA-seq dataset, while the link's relation field claims specifies_fate, which the quote does not support. Two further links, l05 and l12, route pathway -> cell_cell straight past the cell rung with skipped_rung left null, which is the same gap showing up as undeclared bookkeeping.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A perturbation of non-canonical WNT (ligand or receptor) in gliding-mammal patagium dermis, or in mouse lateral dermis, scored for whether the Fp2/Fr fibroblast states form - i.e. an experiment making the pathway responsible for the cell identity, rather than co-detected with it.

verification.method: Python string matching, not reading by eye: every quote and every source document was normalised identically (HTML entities unescaped, XML tags replaced by a space, Unicode dashes and curly quotes folded to ASCII, NBSP folded, all whitespace runs collapsed to one space) and the quote was required to occur as an exact substring of the normalised document. Failures would have been diagnosed by binary-searching the longest matching prefix and by re-searching every other file in the raw directory.

quotes.note: All 19 quotes occur byte-for-byte in the file named in quote_from, under whitespace and XML-tag-boundary normalisation only. No quote was paraphrased, stitched from two places or attributed to the wrong file.

fetch_log.note: Each of the 9 distinct quote_from files resolves to a call in runs/_chains/log/flying-mouse.fetch.json with status 200 and a matching saved_to path. The two documents that failed (PMC1622783, PMC2579364 full text, HTTP 500) are not used as quote_from sources; their abstracts, fetched 200 from NCBI efetch, are, and refused_sources already records the failure and what it cost.

upheld_after_challenge.why: Challenged: the quote hedges ('raised the possibility') and the fetched text names neither species nor cell line for the scratch assay. Upheld because adding recombinant FGF7/FGF10 and measuring a significant increase in migration is a gain of function that changes the process, which is the brief's sufficiency. The caveat stands that the assay involves no identified keratinocytes, no fibroblasts and no patagium, so it does not support the cell_cell entity this link names.

FGF7/FGF10-soaked beads implanted in mouse skin explant, epidermal thickness increased versus PBS: gain of function, correctly graded. Note the relation field says required_for, which is the opposite of what a bead-addition experiment shows; the same relation/grade mismatch appears on l07 and l08.
Doxycycline-inducible Wnt5a double-transgenic with histology and KRT14 IHC: gain of function, correctly graded.
Nog null mouse with failure of webbing regression: loss of function, correctly graded.
Conditional Akirin2 knockout in limb epithelium retaining the interdigital web: loss of function, correctly graded.

Ectopic interdigital Shh from an enhancer-adopting insertion, with CRISPR deletions and a reporter, producing webbing: gain of function, correctly graded, and conservatively so given the reporter and epistasis evidence in that paper.
A comparative growth-rate statement in a review is a correlation, which is what association means, so unlike l18 it was left alone.

walkability.longest_entity_continuous_walk: l01 -> l02 -> l03 -> l07 -> l09 -> l10 spans all seven levels with each link's to-entity matching the next link's from-entity, so the ladder is nominally complete. It is not a walk: it changes species twice (flying squirrel for l01-l03, sugar glider for l07 and l09, bat for l10), every link in it is association except l07, and it terminates at a bat plagiopatagium rather than at any lifting surface on a mouse. No species-continuous walk from molecule to phenotype exists in this ladder, and none exists in a mouse at all.

checks.about: whether the lifting area can hold the mass up
checks.body: asked about powered flight it refuses, and says why the refusal is not pedantry: the question asked is about POWERED flight, and this check cannot answer it. It compares lift with weight at a given airspeed, which is an area question; powered flight is a power question -- whether the flight muscle can supply the induced and profile power through a wingbeat, continuously, at that animal's mass. That needs a coefficient measured through a wingbeat and a muscle power density for the clade, and this repository has neither.

what_is_missing: a lift coefficient measured through a wingbeat cycle, not in a steady glide
a mass-specific mechanical power output for the flight muscle of this clade
a wingbeat frequency and amplitude, or a measurement to fix them
numbers.what_this_can_answer: whether lift carries weight at a stated airspeed, which is a necessary condition for flight of any kind, and so a lower bound on the question asked.

The molecular rungs are LITERATURE in Mus musculus, Petaurus breviceps (sugar glider, Metatheria), complex-tooth flying squirrel (Pteromyidae, Rodentia), Carollia perspicillata (Seba short-tailed bat), bats, species unnamed, in two reviews and one abstract, each link graded and quoted. taxon_audit.headline: Of 737 parts: 79 placed specifically, 165 placed only vacuously, 493 unconstrained, 0 contested, 0 forbidden. Only the first number is evidence that a part belongs in Mus musculus.
taxon_audit.what_it_shows: Taxon constraints cannot do the work the blueprint layer asks of them. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, and for the great majority of parts the ontology either says nothing at all or says only that the part occurs somewhere in a clade containing most of the animal kingdom. That is why a fruit fly came back with bone marrow and a preen gland and without a brain: nothing in the pipeline was ever in a position to object.

verdicts.placed: some in_taxon restriction includes this organism
verdicts.contested: there IS an in_taxon restriction and none includes this organism -- a defect in the blueprint
verdicts.placed-vacuously: the only in_taxon restriction is to a clade in the top third of this organism lineage -- true of it and of most animals, so it discriminates nothing
verdicts.unconstrained: no in_taxon restriction exists, so the ontology is silent; not a defect and not a licence
verdicts.forbidden: never_in_taxon asserts this part cannot be in this organism

laws.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules
laws.because: the quantities are there and no check in this run evaluated this law against them
laws.about: the part graph itself: that each term is a node, each parent relation is one Uberon or CL relation, and the graph has no cycle
laws.how: Structural only. It certifies that the blueprint is a well-formed graph over ontology terms — it says nothing about whether the part could exist, work, or bear a load. It is the one law in the set that reaches every part of every organism, and the weakest thing anyone could want to know about any of them.

laws.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
laws.because: scope.taxa is [Danio rerio], and Mus musculus is in none of them. Its numbers are another clade's.
laws.about: that a claimed developmental ordering has no cycle and respects the dependencies declared for it
laws.how: The only law in the set that is about TIME, which makes it the one the time-lapse rests on. It certifies that an ordering is consistent; it does not supply one, does not predict a rate, and says nothing about how long a stage takes. A developmental animation is therefore a declared ordering being checked for consistency, never a simulation of development.

laws.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
laws.because: scope.taxa is [Danio rerio], and Mus musculus is in none of them. Its numbers are another clade's.
laws.about: what a view of a genotype may omit: that the set shown is closed under the declared pleiotropy relation
laws.how: A statement about the COMPLETENESS OF A VIEW, not about development. If a molecule is shown as affecting one part, this is what certifies that its other declared effects were not quietly dropped from the picture — which is exactly the failure a per-part panel invites.

laws.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance

laws.about: what a claimed set of substitutions rules out, given the genetic code
laws.how: Operates on a claimed edit. For a construct with an unedited donor genome there is nothing for it to operate on, and that is the honest answer rather than a refusal.

E2.label: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
E2.about: a measured band for the weight ratio
E2.how: A measured band from one species. Outside that species it is a number, not a constraint.

E7.label: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
E7.about: that a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored
E7.how: The other law about time, and the one that matters most for a time-lapse: a part that appears after the organism would have died is not a part. Pairs with the developmental ordering law.

aerobic-power-bound.label: Sustained mechanical power is bounded by oxygen delivery (Fick) times efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.about: sustained flight requires aerobic supply at least the required mechanical power over the efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.how: The law that separates a glide from flight. A lifting surface large enough to hold the animal up says nothing about whether the animal can keep it up, and this is the only law in the set that asks. It takes Fick's principle as a NAMED HYPOTHESIS (fick_aerobic_supply) rather than proving it.

fick-principle.label: Fick principle: aerobic supply is at most eta E Q (Ca - Cv)
fick-principle.about: oxygen delivery as flow times the arteriovenous difference
fick-principle.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: the aerobic bound takes it as its named hypothesis fick_aerobic_supply. Everything the aerobic bound concludes rests on it.

physiology-laplace.label: Laplace wall stress: pressure in a thin-walled vessel is limited by wall strength, thickness and radius
physiology-laplace.about: the pressure a thin-walled tube or sphere can hold, from radius, wall thickness and wall strength
physiology-laplace.how: Proved, with NO INSTANCE anywhere in this project: no vessel radius, wall thickness or wall strength exists for any organism here. It is in this table so that a part it would constrain carries the chip that says which three numbers are missing — a law with no instance is a request for data, and silence about it is worse.

E3.label: Efficiency and O2 delivery lie in the ranges the cited sources support (widened after measured zebrafish)
E3.about: a measured ceiling on aerobic power
E3.how: The empirical input the aerobic bound needs. Measured in fish; borrowing it for an insect or a mammal is exactly the move the clade-scoped tables forbid.

scaling-area-law.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
scaling-area-law.about: area under isometry: A scales as L squared
scaling-area-law.how: If the design scales a lifting or exchange surface by changing a length, this fixes the area ratio it gets — under isometry, which is a hypothesis about the design, not a fact about the animal. The flying-fish audit returns `violated` here for skin and fins, because that fish is NOT isometric: the law is right and the hypothesis is false, which is the useful outcome.

E1.label: Isometry fails within a species
E1.about: that measured fin area does not scale isometrically
E1.how: An OBSERVATION of Cypselurus hiraii, not a law. It is the evidence that the isometry hypothesis in the scaling laws is false for that fish, which is why those chips come back `violated` on that body.

scaling-strength-law.label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
scaling-strength-law.about: breaking load under isometry: it scales as L squared while weight scales as L cubed
scaling-strength-law.how: The reason a design cannot simply be made bigger. Weight grows faster than the cross-section carrying it, so a part that holds at one size fails at another with no change in material or shape.

elastic-similarity.label: Elastic similarity scaling (not formalised)
elastic-similarity.about: scaling that holds elastic deflection constant instead of stress
elastic-similarity.how: NOT FORMALISED. The named alternative to isometry for real skeletons, so its absence is why every scaling chip here says `under isometry`.

fin-length-ratio.label: Fin length over body length (not formalised)
fin-length-ratio.about: fin length as a fraction of standard length
fin-length-ratio.how: NOT FORMALISED as a law; E5 records the OBSERVATION that a candidate's ratio falls outside the measured band, which is provenance rather than impossibility.

E5.label: The observed pectoral/SL range
E5.about: a candidate's fin ratio falling outside the measured band
E5.how: PROVENANCE, NOT IMPOSSIBILITY — its own record says so. A design outside a measured band is unusual, and unusual is not forbidden.

muscle-power-premise.label: Thompson's muscle-power premise P = f p M (retired)
muscle-power-premise.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: a named hypothesis (MusclePowerLaw in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean), replaced for the Studio by the aerobic bound. A chip for it must read as an assumption, because that is all it is.

E4.label: Gills do not ventilate in air
E4.about: a measured ceiling on stored (anaerobic) power
E4.how: The burst counterpart of E3: what a muscle can give for a few seconds. For a glide launch this is often the quantity that matters and the one least often declared.

taxiing-thrust.label: Taxiing thrust on the water surface (not formalised)
taxiing-thrust.about: thrust produced while still in contact with the water
taxiing-thrust.how: NOT FORMALISED. The flying-fish runs needed it and did without it.

scaling-bending-law.label: Bending strength of an isometric member via the section modulus (R9)
scaling-bending-law.about: bending stress in a cantilever as the body scales
scaling-bending-law.how: A wing or a leg held out from the body is a cantilever, and the stress at its root rises with size under isometry. This is the law that should be consulted first by anyone who wants to put a lifting surface on the end of a limb.

walking-pendulum-speed.label: Walking speed as a pendulum (not formalised)
walking-pendulum-speed.about: the speed at which a leg of a given length stops working as a pendulum
walking-pendulum-speed.how: NOT FORMALISED. The locomotion layer reports a Froude number for a walking gait and calls the verdict `reported` rather than a pass, precisely because this is missing.

genotype-pleiotropy-closure.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.about: what a view of a genotype may omit: that the set shown is closed under the declared pleiotropy relation
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.how: A statement about the COMPLETENESS OF A VIEW, not about development. If a molecule is shown as affecting one part, this is what certifies that its other declared effects were not quietly dropped from the picture — which is exactly the failure a per-part panel invites.

genotype-genetic-code.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
genotype-genetic-code.about: what a claimed set of substitutions rules out, given the genetic code
genotype-genetic-code.how: Operates on a claimed edit. For a construct with an unedited donor genome there is nothing for it to operate on, and that is the honest answer rather than a refusal.

gene-regulatory-dynamics.label: Gene regulatory dynamics (not formalised)
gene-regulatory-dynamics.about: the dynamics of a regulatory network
gene-regulatory-dynamics.how: NOT FORMALISED, and it is the hole the whole scale ladder sits over. Nothing in the Lean set connects a molecule to a tissue. The ladder's molecular rungs are therefore LITERATURE, graded and quoted, and the theatre must never draw them in the same colour as a proof.

thompson1917-ch02-10.label: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
thompson1917-ch02-10.about: how minimum flight speed scales with size
thompson1917-ch02-10.how: A bigger animal of the same shape must fly faster to stay up. Combined with a launch speed the design declares, this is often what decides a flight claim.

flight-allometry-law.label: General allometry: measured exponents compose (W = a L^b)
flight-allometry-law.about: minimum speed from wing loading and a maximum lift coefficient
flight-allometry-law.how: The law behind `lifting_area_supports_mass`. It needs a maximum lift coefficient, which is where a design most often stops: the coefficient is a MEASURED property of a real wing, the table of them is scoped by clade, and borrowing one across clades is the failure that table exists to prevent.

flight-climb-glide-law.label: Climb from excess power and the range of a steady glide
flight-climb-glide-law.about: climb rate from excess power, and the horizontal range of a steady glide from a height
flight-climb-glide-law.how: Scope.taxa is `any`: it is a theorem about a model and applies wherever the design supplies the quantities and accepts the hypotheses. That makes it the most portable flight law here — and it is about a GLIDE. Powered flight is a power question and goes to the aerobic bound.

aspect-ratio-induced-drag.label: Induced drag falls with wing aspect ratio (not formalised)
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.about: induced drag falling with aspect ratio
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.how: NOT FORMALISED. Without it, nothing here distinguishes a long narrow wing from a short broad one of the same area, which is most of what a wing design IS.

universal_laws.because: the quantities are there and no check in this run evaluated this law against them
scope.taxa is [Danio rerio], and Mus musculus is in none of them. Its numbers are another clade's.
scope.taxa is [Danio rerio], and Mus musculus is in none of them. Its numbers are another clade's.

Pathway and cell are joined only by appearing in the same snRNA-seq dataset, while the link's relation field claims specifies_fate, which the quote does not support. Two further links, l05 and l12, route pathway -> cell_cell straight past the cell rung with skipped_rung left null, which is the same gap showing up as undeclared bookkeeping.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A perturbation of non-canonical WNT (ligand or receptor) in gliding-mammal patagium dermis, or in mouse lateral dermis, scored for whether the Fp2/Fr fibroblast states form - i.e. an experiment making the pathway responsible for the cell identity, rather than co-detected with it.

verification.method: Python string matching, not reading by eye: every quote and every source document was normalised identically (HTML entities unescaped, XML tags replaced by a space, Unicode dashes and curly quotes folded to ASCII, NBSP folded, all whitespace runs collapsed to one space) and the quote was required to occur as an exact substring of the normalised document. Failures would have been diagnosed by binary-searching the longest matching prefix and by re-searching every other file in the raw directory.

quotes.note: All 19 quotes occur byte-for-byte in the file named in quote_from, under whitespace and XML-tag-boundary normalisation only. No quote was paraphrased, stitched from two places or attributed to the wrong file.

fetch_log.note: Each of the 9 distinct quote_from files resolves to a call in runs/_chains/log/flying-mouse.fetch.json with status 200 and a matching saved_to path. The two documents that failed (PMC1622783, PMC2579364 full text, HTTP 500) are not used as quote_from sources; their abstracts, fetched 200 from NCBI efetch, are, and refused_sources already records the failure and what it cost.

upheld_after_challenge.why: Challenged: the quote hedges ('raised the possibility') and the fetched text names neither species nor cell line for the scratch assay. Upheld because adding recombinant FGF7/FGF10 and measuring a significant increase in migration is a gain of function that changes the process, which is the brief's sufficiency. The caveat stands that the assay involves no identified keratinocytes, no fibroblasts and no patagium, so it does not support the cell_cell entity this link names.

FGF7/FGF10-soaked beads implanted in mouse skin explant, epidermal thickness increased versus PBS: gain of function, correctly graded. Note the relation field says required_for, which is the opposite of what a bead-addition experiment shows; the same relation/grade mismatch appears on l07 and l08.
Doxycycline-inducible Wnt5a double-transgenic with histology and KRT14 IHC: gain of function, correctly graded.
Nog null mouse with failure of webbing regression: loss of function, correctly graded.
Conditional Akirin2 knockout in limb epithelium retaining the interdigital web: loss of function, correctly graded.

Ectopic interdigital Shh from an enhancer-adopting insertion, with CRISPR deletions and a reporter, producing webbing: gain of function, correctly graded, and conservatively so given the reporter and epistasis evidence in that paper.
A comparative growth-rate statement in a review is a correlation, which is what association means, so unlike l18 it was left alone.

walkability.longest_entity_continuous_walk: l01 -> l02 -> l03 -> l07 -> l09 -> l10 spans all seven levels with each link's to-entity matching the next link's from-entity, so the ladder is nominally complete. It is not a walk: it changes species twice (flying squirrel for l01-l03, sugar glider for l07 and l09, bat for l10), every link in it is association except l07, and it terminates at a bat plagiopatagium rather than at any lifting surface on a mouse. No species-continuous walk from molecule to phenotype exists in this ladder, and none exists in a mouse at all.

numbers.caveat: This document names a TAXON and carries a DECLARED parameter set: quantities the designer stated, each with a source saying where it came from. Nobody measured them on this organism, and the engine holds measured parameters only for the organisms in its bundle. Every declared value enters STATE with kind "assumed", so the weakest-input machinery and every model_confidence downstream carry the fact that a person stated it. A result computed from them is a statement about those declarations as much as about the organism; fields nobody declared stay null and the checks that need them still refuse.

the engine has no geometry for it: STATE carries areas and a span but no longitudinal positions, and the mesh manifests carry only a per-object centre, which is neither a planform AREA CENTROID nor a CENTRE OF MASS. Estimating the margin from that object centre gives about -43 % MAC for the adult flying fish against the -7.7 % MEASURED by anatomy-model/print/balance_1to1.py on a real 1:1 flying-fish mesh, a factor of five on the one instance available, so no number is reported here.

checks.body: the aerodynamic verdict now comes out of the FULL pipeline rather than a check called by hand: 70.0 cm2 against the 34.2 cm2 needed, with C_Lmax 1.48 taken by clade and labelled borrowed. Same number as generation 2 reached directly, by a different route, which is the point: the layers agree because they share one coefficient policy.

detail.launch_airspeed_from: supplied in STATE (assumed: DECLARED by the design, not measured: DESIGN INPUT: sqrt(2gh) for the h = 4 m launch height Bishop 2006 used for Glaucomys volans, ignoring drag, so an upper bound on what a drop can give. Not a measured airspeed of anything.)
detail.C_Lmax_note: C_Lmax 1.48 is BORROWED: it was measured on live Petaurus breviceps (sugar glider, a marsupial) in free glides, mean angle of attack 44.15 +/- 3.12 deg and is applied here to Mus musculus because the NCBI taxonomy places both inside Theria <mammals>. Measured in a marsupial glider and offered across Theria, which is marsupials and placentals together. For any taxon other than Petaurus breviceps this is a BORROW across a clade, and the check labels it so. It is the closest measurement in this repository to a gliding mammal; it is not a measurement of the animal being designed. Taxon Mus musculus, from stated on the design.
detail.C_Lmax_caveat: THIS IS A STALLED-MEMBRANE GLIDE COEFFICIENT, NOT A STEADY-FLIGHT MAXIMUM, and the source is explicit that it was not enough. In the same glides the animals accelerated downward at 1.0 +/- 0.5 m/s2 and forward at 2.1 +/- 0.6 m/s2: Bishop states that body weight was NOT fully supported by aerodynamic force and that some of the lift went into forward acceleration. The angles of attack are far above where an engineered wing stalls. Bishop KL 2006 (J Exp Biol 209:689-701, doi 10.1242/jeb.02062) reports the same for Glaucomys volans, gliding at 35.4-53.5 deg with the wings stalled and accelerating downward, and finds flying squirrels reach higher lift coefficients than sugar gliders -- so 1.48 is, if anything, generous for a mammal without a flying squirrel's specialisations.
detail.C_Lmax_source: Bishop KL 2007, Aerodynamic force generation, performance and control of body orientation during gliding in sugar gliders (Petaurus breviceps), J Exp Biol 210:2593-2606
detail.area_convention: STATE lifting_area_m2 is pectoral + pelvic + caudal (mesh); the coefficient is referred to the whole outstretched body-and-membrane planform, as digitised from the gliding animal. The conventions differ and this check does not correct for it.

honesty: 5 part(s) are named by the literature chain and ABSENT from the blueprint (fibroblast, dermis, patagium, interdigital region, forelimb). They are drawn as ghosts, marked blueprint_has_it: false. For the fruit fly these are the very organs the longevity experiments act in.
The 13 molecules are marker annotations from the Protein Ontology, carried by the blueprint. None of them was measured in this organism and none is evidence of function.

The molecular rungs are LITERATURE in Mus musculus, Petaurus breviceps (sugar glider, Metatheria), complex-tooth flying squirrel (Pteromyidae, Rodentia), Carollia perspicillata (Seba short-tailed bat), bats, species unnamed, in two reviews and one abstract, each link graded and quoted. Only five links (l06, l08, l13, l14, l15) are mouse data, and every one of them is either ordinary trunk-skin thickening or a syndactyly defect; all patagium and wing evidence comes from a marsupial sugar glider, a rodent flying squirrel and bats, and none of it is data from a mouse that flies, because no such animal exists.

Rung organ -> phenotype is MISSING: Nothing fetched in this run relates a membrane area to the body mass it can support. The physics layer's lifting_area_supports_mass: met used a DECLARED area; the one aerodynamic statement found (l18) is a narrative review sentence with no numbers, and the bat review that does discuss wing loading and wing area reports them only as postnatal growth curves for bats, never as a threshold a mouse-sized animal would have to clear.

Rung molecule -> organ is MISSING: No mouse genotype in anything fetched produces a patagium or any membrane that spans a joint. The strongest mouse gain-of-function found (l08, inducible Wnt5a) thickens and densifies skin everywhere at once; the strongest mouse routes to webbing (l13, l14, l15) are syndactyly defects of the autopod. The gap between skin gets thicker, or digits stay fused, and a lifting surface exists is not crossed by any document fetched here.

Rung cell_cell -> tissue is MISSING: In the bat, the species whose anatomy the design actually wants, the dermal-epidermal step cannot be tested: the authors state that reliance on field-collected embryos prevented in vivo or explant tests of WNT5A function. So the bat side of the ladder stops at association (l10) and never reaches necessity.

Rung cell -> cell_cell is MISSING: The flying squirrel fibroblast-to-keratinocyte interaction (l03) is a CellChat inference from single-nucleus transcriptomes, which the paper itself labels putative and candidate. Nothing fetched perturbs a receptor on the keratinocyte side in any gliding mammal.

Rung tissue -> organ is MISSING: No document fetched gives any mechanical property of a retained interdigital web or of a patagium: no tensile strength, stiffness, thickness under load or failure point. A membrane that exists is not yet a membrane that bears a body.

Rung molecule -> pathway is MISSING: The ontology layer does not grant the designed organism the structure it needs, so the ladder cannot be named end to end. Querying Ubergraph in this run returned wing (UBERON_0000023) never_in_taxon Glires (NCBITaxon_314147) and never_in_taxon Metatheria (NCBITaxon_9263), while two of the three patagium papers fetched here describe gliding membranes in exactly those clades - a rodent flying squirrel and a marsupial sugar glider. patagium (UBERON_0010856) itself returned no never_in_taxon rows in this run. A mouse is Glires, so per the fetched axioms it is forbidden a wing.

Rung pathway -> cell is MISSING: Found by adversarial verification, not declared by the builder. The pathway -> cell rung is occupied by exactly one link, l02, and l02 does not cross it. Its quote reports only that two fibroblast subpopulations (Fp2, Fr) are patagium-enriched by differential abundance and expression; the link's own what_it_does_not_show concedes 'nothing here shows the WNT pathway is required to produce them'. Pathway and cell are joined only by appearing in the same snRNA-seq dataset, while the link's relation field claims specifies_fate, which the quote does not support. Two further links, l05 and l12, route pathway -> cell_cell straight past the cell rung with skipped_rung left null, which is the same gap showing up as undeclared bookkeeping.
431 law chips are out of scope for this organism: the law is about the right quantity and its numbers belong to another clade.

THE ONTOLOGY BARELY PLACES THIS BODY IN THIS ORGANISM. Of 737 parts the blueprint returned, 79 have an in_taxon restriction specific enough to be evidence that Mus musculus has them; 165 are restricted only to a clade containing most of the animal kingdom, and 493 carry no restriction at all. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, so most of what is drawn here is unevidenced rather than wrong.
No part in this view has measured geometry. Every position is a declared slot in sim-engine/scales/body-frames.json, and a shape is a primitive, not a morphology.

taxon_audit.headline: Of 737 parts: 79 placed specifically, 165 placed only vacuously, 493 unconstrained, 0 contested, 0 forbidden. Only the first number is evidence that a part belongs in Mus musculus.
taxon_audit.what_it_shows: Taxon constraints cannot do the work the blueprint layer asks of them. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, and for the great majority of parts the ontology either says nothing at all or says only that the part occurs somewhere in a clade containing most of the animal kingdom. That is why a fruit fly came back with bone marrow and a preen gland and without a brain: nothing in the pipeline was ever in a position to object.

verdicts.placed: some in_taxon restriction includes this organism
verdicts.contested: there IS an in_taxon restriction and none includes this organism -- a defect in the blueprint
verdicts.placed-vacuously: the only in_taxon restriction is to a clade in the top third of this organism lineage -- true of it and of most animals, so it discriminates nothing
verdicts.unconstrained: no in_taxon restriction exists, so the ontology is silent; not a defect and not a licence
verdicts.forbidden: never_in_taxon asserts this part cannot be in this organism

4.what_it_taught: The refusals in generation 0 were not about the mouse. organism_get and physics_check refused because a taxon base resolved no STATE, and a design that declares its quantities -- with sources, as every other check in this repository already required -- resolves one. physics_check now runs on a mouse and each standing check that still cannot answer names the field it wanted. The aerodynamic verdict agrees with the one generation 2 got by calling the check directly.

missing_rungs.why: Nothing fetched in this run relates a membrane area to the body mass it can support. The physics layer's lifting_area_supports_mass: met used a DECLARED area; the one aerodynamic statement found (l18) is a narrative review sentence with no numbers, and the bat review that does discuss wing loading and wing area reports them only as postnatal growth curves for bats, never as a threshold a mouse-sized animal would have to clear.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A measured wing-area / body-mass (wing loading) dataset for small mammals, with a stated minimum area for a 20-30 g body, so the declared area could be checked rather than assumed.

missing_rungs.why: No mouse genotype in anything fetched produces a patagium or any membrane that spans a joint. The strongest mouse gain-of-function found (l08, inducible Wnt5a) thickens and densifies skin everywhere at once; the strongest mouse routes to webbing (l13, l14, l15) are syndactyly defects of the autopod. The gap between skin gets thicker, or digits stay fused, and a lifting surface exists is not crossed by any document fetched here.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A spatially restricted gain-of-function mouse - for example Wnt5a, or Fgf7 and Fgf10, driven in interlimb lateral dermis or in forelimb interdigital mesenchyme - scored for membrane outgrowth, area and span. This run found no record of such an experiment.

missing_rungs.why: In the bat, the species whose anatomy the design actually wants, the dermal-epidermal step cannot be tested: the authors state that reliance on field-collected embryos prevented in vivo or explant tests of WNT5A function. So the bat side of the ladder stops at association (l10) and never reaches necessity.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A bat embryo culture or electroporation system, or a captive breeding colony, allowing loss of function of Wnt5a or of the FGF7/FGF10 axis in the developing plagiopatagium.

missing_rungs.why: The flying squirrel fibroblast-to-keratinocyte interaction (l03) is a CellChat inference from single-nucleus transcriptomes, which the paper itself labels putative and candidate. Nothing fetched perturbs a receptor on the keratinocyte side in any gliding mammal.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Receptor-side perturbation, for example FGFR2 or a non-canonical WNT receptor, in patagium epidermis, with the dermal condensate and epidermal thickness scored.

missing_rungs.why: No document fetched gives any mechanical property of a retained interdigital web or of a patagium: no tensile strength, stiffness, thickness under load or failure point. A membrane that exists is not yet a membrane that bears a body.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Mechanical testing of patagium, and of retained interdigital webbing in the mouse syndactyly models above, against the aerodynamic load implied by the physics layer's 4 m drop.

missing_rungs.why: The ontology layer does not grant the designed organism the structure it needs, so the ladder cannot be named end to end. Querying Ubergraph in this run returned wing (UBERON_0000023) never_in_taxon Glires (NCBITaxon_314147) and never_in_taxon Metatheria (NCBITaxon_9263), while two of the three patagium papers fetched here describe gliding membranes in exactly those clades - a rodent flying squirrel and a marsupial sugar glider. patagium (UBERON_0010856) itself returned no never_in_taxon rows in this run. A mouse is Glires, so per the fetched axioms it is forbidden a wing.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Either an Uberon revision removing or narrowing the wing never_in_taxon Glires and Metatheria axioms, or a decision in this project to land the mouse ladder on patagium rather than wing.

missing_rungs.why: Found by adversarial verification, not declared by the builder. The pathway -> cell rung is occupied by exactly one link, l02, and l02 does not cross it. Its quote reports only that two fibroblast subpopulations (Fp2, Fr) are patagium-enriched by differential abundance and expression; the link's own what_it_does_not_show concedes 'nothing here shows the WNT pathway is required to produce them'. Pathway and cell are joined only by appearing in the same snRNA-seq dataset, while the link's relation field claims specifies_fate, which the quote does not support. Two further links, l05 and l12, route pathway -> cell_cell straight past the cell rung with skipped_rung left null, which is the same gap showing up as undeclared bookkeeping.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A perturbation of non-canonical WNT (ligand or receptor) in gliding-mammal patagium dermis, or in mouse lateral dermis, scored for whether the Fp2/Fr fibroblast states form - i.e. an experiment making the pathway responsible for the cell identity, rather than co-detected with it.

verification.method: Python string matching, not reading by eye: every quote and every source document was normalised identically (HTML entities unescaped, XML tags replaced by a space, Unicode dashes and curly quotes folded to ASCII, NBSP folded, all whitespace runs collapsed to one space) and the quote was required to occur as an exact substring of the normalised document. Failures would have been diagnosed by binary-searching the longest matching prefix and by re-searching every other file in the raw directory.

quotes.note: All 19 quotes occur byte-for-byte in the file named in quote_from, under whitespace and XML-tag-boundary normalisation only. No quote was paraphrased, stitched from two places or attributed to the wrong file.

fetch_log.note: Each of the 9 distinct quote_from files resolves to a call in runs/_chains/log/flying-mouse.fetch.json with status 200 and a matching saved_to path. The two documents that failed (PMC1622783, PMC2579364 full text, HTTP 500) are not used as quote_from sources; their abstracts, fetched 200 from NCBI efetch, are, and refused_sources already records the failure and what it cost.

upheld_after_challenge.why: Challenged: the quote hedges ('raised the possibility') and the fetched text names neither species nor cell line for the scratch assay. Upheld because adding recombinant FGF7/FGF10 and measuring a significant increase in migration is a gain of function that changes the process, which is the brief's sufficiency. The caveat stands that the assay involves no identified keratinocytes, no fibroblasts and no patagium, so it does not support the cell_cell entity this link names.

FGF7/FGF10-soaked beads implanted in mouse skin explant, epidermal thickness increased versus PBS: gain of function, correctly graded. Note the relation field says required_for, which is the opposite of what a bead-addition experiment shows; the same relation/grade mismatch appears on l07 and l08.
Doxycycline-inducible Wnt5a double-transgenic with histology and KRT14 IHC: gain of function, correctly graded.
Nog null mouse with failure of webbing regression: loss of function, correctly graded.
Conditional Akirin2 knockout in limb epithelium retaining the interdigital web: loss of function, correctly graded.

Ectopic interdigital Shh from an enhancer-adopting insertion, with CRISPR deletions and a reporter, producing webbing: gain of function, correctly graded, and conservatively so given the reporter and epistasis evidence in that paper.
A comparative growth-rate statement in a review is a correlation, which is what association means, so unlike l18 it was left alone.

walkability.longest_entity_continuous_walk: l01 -> l02 -> l03 -> l07 -> l09 -> l10 spans all seven levels with each link's to-entity matching the next link's from-entity, so the ladder is nominally complete. It is not a walk: it changes species twice (flying squirrel for l01-l03, sugar glider for l07 and l09, bat for l10), every link in it is association except l07, and it terminates at a bat plagiopatagium rather than at any lifting surface on a mouse. No species-continuous walk from molecule to phenotype exists in this ladder, and none exists in a mouse at all.
